column1: # Capture targets: node hash <TAB> page path
# ONE PAGE PER NODE. Not one per pass, not one per day. One.
# An earlier draft listed rngit's twelve other paths as a "second pass on
# another day". That is crawling with extra steps: walking every path a node
# exposes is the behaviour the maintainer objected to, and spreading it over
# days changes the interval, not the thing.
# WHERE THE PATHS CAME FROM, which is the part that matters. Not from asking
# these nodes what they serve. Roogle already crawled them and publishes the
# result, so its index answered "what pages does Aleph have" at zero cost to
# Aleph:
#   curl -A '<who you are>' 'https://roogle.us/api/v1/node?node=<hash>&format=tsv&snippet=0'
# That is discovery without probing, and it also lets each node be asked for its
# single most useful page instead of index by default.
# Roogle's own etiquette, which this follows: identify yourself in the
# User-Agent, cache, back off on 429, and if you want bulk data ask for a dump
# rather than paging the whole index.
